source: postico-beekeeper lens — Postico 2 (v2.3.3, Feb 2026: eggerapps.at docs + releases.eggerapps.at changelog + GitHub jakob/Postico issues) and Beekeeper Studio (v5.x through 2026: docs.beekeeperstudio.io, release blogs 5.0/5.2/5.4, GitHub issues #135/#752/#1857/#698, G2/SaaSHub reviews)

findings.title: Quick Filter Actions: right-click a value to filter by it (Postico 2.2)
findings.detail: Right-click any cell → 'show only rows with this value' / 'hide rows with this value'. Loved because it turns exploration into zero-typing filtering — you see an interesting value and pivot instantly. Beyond: make quick-filters stackable chips above the grid (each removable), support multi-cell selection → IN-list filter, offer 'filter by prefix/contains' variants for text, and make it work on arbitrary query results by rewriting the WHERE (qwry already traces result columns to origin tables for edit-from-SQL — reuse that plumbing).

findings.title: Foreign key picker when editing FK cells (Postico)
findings.detail: Editing a cell that's an FK opens a searchable picker of referenced-table rows instead of forcing you to memorize ids. Widely cited as what makes 'editing all kinds of tables a breeze'. Beyond: keyset-paginated type-to-search picker (<16ms per keystroke), display-column heuristic (first text/name-like column shown next to the PK), recent-picks at top, and Esc leaves the cell untouched. No competitor makes the picker fast on 1M-row referenced tables — qwry can.

findings.title: Clickable foreign keys / goto referenced row (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: FK values are clickable and jump to the referenced row; Query Magics even has __format__goto for arbitrary columns. Loved because FK-hopping is the core browse loop. Beyond: ⌘-click an FK value → peek popover of the referenced row (inspector-style, no tab churn), full-click opens filtered browse in a new tab, plus the reverse — 'show rows referencing this' using pg_constraint backlinks. Maintain a per-tab nav stack so ⌥⌘←/→ walks back through hops (Postico's Finder-like history).

findings.title: Row detail sidebar for long values and images (Postico)
findings.detail: Selecting a cell shows the full value in a sidebar — long text, images from bytea — so wide values never fight the grid. qwry's Inspector is the analog. Beyond: render images (bytea magic-number sniff + URL detection), bytea encoding switcher (Hex/Base64/Crockford Base32/ULID — Postico 2.1.2 shipped exactly this and users asked for it), and make the sidebar a first-class editor sharing the staged-edit pipeline, not a viewer.

findings.title: Row-as-JSON sidebar with FKs as nested data (Beekeeper 5.2)
findings.detail: View any row as clean structured JSON with foreign keys expanded as nested objects; 5.2 made it editable, made it work on query results, and auto-detects JSON stored in text/varchar. Beyond: qwry's jsonb-first inspector should add whole-row JSON mode with lazy FK expansion (click to fetch referenced row inline), copy-row-as-JSON, and edits in the JSON view staging back through the normal edit pipeline. Critically gate auto-JSON-detection on actual parse + column type — qwry's known structuredValue bug ('[draft]' text treated as JSON) is exactly the corruption Beekeeper risks.

findings.title: Staged deletes are visible and undoable before save (Postico)
findings.detail: Rows marked for deletion render struck-through and can be 'undeleted' before ⌘S commits (added 2.0.2 by user demand). Loved because it makes the staging model legible — you always see what will happen. Beyond: a pending-changes panel listing every staged INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE as human-readable rows AND as the exact SQL, with per-row revert. This is the 'never lies about data' invariant given a UI.

findings.title: 'Copy To SQL' for staged edits (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Instead of applying pending changes, one button converts them to SQL in a new editor tab for review/tweaking. Power users love it — it converts GUI trust into SQL trust. Beyond: qwry already generates UPDATEs from edits; add 'Review as SQL' that opens the generated statements wrapped in BEGIN/COMMIT with the affected-row count as a comment per statement, editable and runnable. Also do it in reverse: after apply, offer 'copy what was executed'.

findings.title: Color-coded pending-change states + Apply/Reset bar (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Green=new, orange=edited, red=deleted, with a persistent Apply/Reset bar showing the count. Legibility of dirty state is why the staged model feels safe. Beyond: qwry has dirty-cell flash; add a persistent count pill ('3 changes' → click = changes panel), per-cell tint that survives scroll, and Esc-to-revert-cell vs ⌘Z stepping back individual stages.

findings.title: Multi-column sort via Option+click + per-column NULLS FIRST/LAST (Postico 2.1)
findings.detail: Option-click a header adds a secondary sort; the header context menu sets NULL ordering. Small but constantly praised — real datasets need tiebreakers. Beyond: shift-click adds sort with ordinal badges (1,2,3) on headers, NULLS control in the header menu, and the whole sort/filter state compiles to a visible ORDER BY users can copy into the editor. Also serialize sort into the browse SQL so keyset pagination stays correct (qwry roadmap already flags the PK-tiebreaker need).

findings.title: Filter bar with GUI conditions + raw-SQL escape hatch (both apps)
findings.detail: Beekeeper: per-column dropdown (=, >, <, LIKE, IN) plus a '<>' toggle that switches to raw WHERE-clause text. Postico: 'is in list' filter and 'Custom SQL' filters. Loved because the GUI covers 90% and the escape hatch covers the rest without leaving the view. Beyond: token/chip filters that always show the compiled WHERE as a live one-line SQL preview (click = pop into editor), paste a newline/comma list into a filter → auto IN-list, and per-type operators (jsonb @>, array ANY, ILIKE default for text). Apply on Enter, not per keystroke — qwry's current per-char re-query is the anti-pattern.

findings.title: Open Quickly: ⌘P fuzzy jump to any table (Postico)
findings.detail: ⌘P fuzzy-searches tables and jumps straight to content — the single most-used navigation in Postico. Beekeeper 5.2's quick-search additionally lists open tabs (VSCode-style). Beyond: qwry's palette should rank by recency+frequency, index tables/views/columns/functions/saved-queries/open-tabs in one list with type glyphs, support schema-qualified fuzzy ('pub ord' → public.orders), and guarantee <16ms per keystroke on a 5k-table catalog — Beekeeper measurably fails at this scale (1200 tables ≈ 1min sidebar load, GitHub #135).

findings.title: Navigation history: back/forward + up/down hierarchy (Postico)
findings.detail: ⌥⌘←/→ walk back/forward through visited tables/views like Finder; ⌥⌘↑/↓ move up/down the hierarchy. Makes the browser feel like a native file manager. Beyond: per-tab history stack that also records filter/sort/scroll state and FK hops (back returns you to the exact row), plus two-finger trackpad swipe. No SQL client does swipe-back; it's a very mac-native touch.

findings.title: In-place query history scrubbing: ^⌘←/→ replaces editor with prev/next query (Postico)
findings.detail: Like shell up-arrow: cycle previous executed queries directly in the editor. Beloved by psql refugees. Beyond: add ⌃R reverse-i-search over history (type fragment, see matches inline), and a history ghost — when the editor is empty, faintly show the last query with 'press ↑ to restore'. Pairs with a persistent indexed history (below).

findings.title: Indexed, searchable query history across all sessions (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Every executed query is persisted to local SQLite and searchable from a history panel — 'an indexed query history you can search across all past sessions'. This is never-lose-work applied to SQL itself. Beyond: FTS over history with per-connection filter, dedupe of identical reruns (keep run count + last timing), click = restore to a new tab, and show rows-affected/duration per entry. Store locally, no cloud — matches qwry's local-only stance while Beekeeper gates edit-history behind paid workspaces.

findings.title: Current-statement highlight + execute-current vs execute-all (Postico)
findings.detail: The statement under the cursor is highlighted light grey; ⌘↩ runs just it, ⌥⌘↩ runs all, and multi-statement selections run in an implicit transaction with rollback on failure. The grey highlight is the affordance — you always know what ⌘↩ will do. Beyond: same subtle highlight plus a gutter run-glyph per statement, and surface the implicit-transaction behavior explicitly ('3 statements · runs atomically') so rollback-on-failure is a promise, not a surprise.

findings.title: psql-style Tab completion with grouped, collapsible suggestions (Postico)
findings.detail: Tab cycles completions like bash/psql; Ctrl-Space/Esc shows the full list; suggestions are grouped (tables/columns/functions) and groups expand/collapse with arrow keys. CLI muscle-memory in a GUI is why editors feel 'for me'. Beyond: qwry's schema-aware intellisense already wins on substance; add Tab-cycle as an optional mode, group headers in the completion popup, and alias-aware column completion ordering (columns of FROM-clause tables first).

findings.title: Built-in pgFormatter honoring ~/.pg_format (Postico)
findings.detail: Ctrl-F formats SQL locally via bundled pgFormatter, respecting the user's ~/.pg_format config — no network, instant, and consistent with their CLI setup. Beyond: format-selection-only, format-on-paste option, and a style picker (keyword case, comma-first) persisted per user; keep it <50ms local. Reading ~/.pg_format if present is a cheap 'we respect your existing tools' win.

findings.title: Query parameters with prompt-on-run (:var, $1, ?) (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Placeholders in queries trigger a value prompt at execution; syntax configurable per database. Loved for shareable parameterized snippets and avoiding string-editing between runs. Beyond: remember last values per query, type-infer the input widget from context (date picker for timestamp comparisons), named parameter sets ('staging ids' vs 'prod ids'), and run them as real extended-protocol parameters — which also kills injection in a way Beekeeper's string substitution doesn't.

findings.title: Query Magics: alias-suffix rendering of links/images/money/progress/stars/enum/goto (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: SELECT price AS price__format__money__gbp renders currency; __format__image renders thumbnails; __format__goto__users makes cells navigate. Genuinely novel and loved for dashboards-from-SQL. But the alias hack pollutes the query. Beyond: qwry can render from pg types + header right-click 'Display as ▸' menu (link, image, money, checkmark, unixtime, progress) persisted per column — same payoff, zero query rewriting, and it works on any query without magic strings.

findings.title: Edit-in-modal for JSON/long values with syntax checking (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Right-click cell → 'Edit in Modal' opens a pop-out editor with syntax highlighting and validation because 'editing a JSON document in a tiny table cell isn't a great experience'. Beyond: qwry's jsonb-first inspector already beats the modal; add a diff-vs-original toggle before staging, JSON5-tolerant input with canonical output, and validation against the column's CHECK constraints where determinable.

findings.title: Copy in many formats, done correctly (both)
findings.detail: Beekeeper: CSV/JSON/Markdown/Excel-formatted/SQL-insert from any selection. Postico: 'Copy as Markdown' (2.0 RC3), copy INSERT without E'' escape literals (2.2 — a correctness refinement users noticed), 'Copy Name with Schema', copy single column value. The density and correctness of copy is what 'mature' feels like. Beyond: one Copy ▸ submenu everywhere (cell/selection/row/column/table) with TSV-for-Excel, JSON array + NDJSON, IN-list, INSERT with the real table name (qwry's current your_table bug), UPDATE-shaped, and psql \copy form. Type-aware quoting: numerics bare, NULLs as NULL not 'NULL'.

findings.title: IN-clause generation from selected values (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Select cells in a column → copy as SQL IN (...) clause. Tiny feature, constantly used for 'now query these ids elsewhere'. Beyond: type-aware quoting, NULL exclusion with an 'excluded 2 NULLs' toast, and a sibling action 'Filter this table by selection' that applies the IN-list as a grid filter chip directly.

findings.title: Column hide/show + resize-all + width persistence (both)
findings.detail: Beekeeper: hide column via header right-click, resize all columns at once. Postico 2.0.5: column widths persist per table. Loved because wide tables are the norm and re-fiddling widths every open is death by a thousand cuts. Beyond: persist width/visibility/sort per table per connection, ⌥-double-click divider = fit-all-to-content (sampled, not full-scan), and a column list popover with checkboxes + type icons for bulk show/hide.

findings.title: Pinned tables at the top of the sidebar with persistent state (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Pin most-used tables/views; pins survive restarts. Users praise it because real work touches ~5 of 500 tables. Beyond: pin tables AND saved queries into a per-connection 'workspace' strip, drag-reorderable, with pins stored in the same syncable favorites file as connections. Auto-suggest pins from open frequency.

findings.title: Tab session restore + reopen-closed-tab + reorder (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Tabs (with content) persist between sessions; 5.2 added ⌘⇧T-style 'reopen recently closed tabs'; tabs reorder by drag. This is the 'my workspace is still there' feeling users cite when choosing Beekeeper. Beyond: restore tabs with cursor position, scroll offset, and last-result metadata ('ran 2h ago · 1,204 rows'); a reopen-closed stack (multiple levels); auto-title tabs from SQL (SELECT orders → 'orders'); pin tabs. qwry's never-lose-work invariant makes this table stakes.

findings.title: Saved queries: one-keystroke save, folders, and the Postico cautionary tale
findings.detail: Beekeeper: ⌘S names-and-saves to local SQLite, organized in folders, searchable. Postico 2 went further — every query is a saved file with autosave, folders, symlinks, external-editor compatibility — and got its top complaint for it: GitHub #698 'one-off queries are clumsy', users mourn Postico 1's one-click scratch query. Lesson: scratch-first, save-optional. Beyond for qwry: ⌘T instantly gives an unnamed autosaved scratch tab (never prompts, never nags), ⌘S promotes it to a named saved query; scratch tabs are still session-restored and history-indexed so nothing is ever lost — the safety of Postico's model without its ceremony.

findings.title: Automatic version history for saved queries (Beekeeper workspaces)
findings.detail: Cloud workspaces record every edit to a query with compare-and-rollback. Beloved concept, but paywalled and cloud-only. Beyond: local automatic snapshots on every save/run with a diff viewer and one-click restore — qwry can ship Beekeeper's paid feature free and offline, directly serving never-lose-work.

findings.title: Multiple result sets with a selector (both)
findings.detail: Run several statements → Postico shows a bottom-left popup to flip between results; Beekeeper a dropdown. Beyond: one result strip with a chip per statement (verb + table + row count + duration), keyboard cycling, and keep the previous run's results per tab so you can flip between 'this run' and 'last run' — nobody offers cheap before/after comparison of a query you're iterating on.

findings.title: Honest result truncation with visible cap (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Results truncate at 50k rows 'to preserve memory' and say so. Users respect honesty; they hate silent truncation. Beyond: qwry's 50k in-memory cap should read 'showing 50,000 of ~1.2M (estimated)' with keyset load-more, and find-in-results must display 'found 12 in loaded rows only' (already on the roadmap — this census confirms it's the right call). Never look broken; never lie.

findings.title: Streaming export: Run-To-File + timestamped filename suggestions
findings.detail: Beekeeper's 'Run To File' streams a query straight to CSV without rendering (paid); Postico 2.2.2 auto-suggests timestamp-based filenames for result exports. Beyond: free streaming export to CSV/NDJSON/JSON with a progress bar + cancel, default filename {table}_{yyyymmdd_hhmm}.csv, and 'export what I see' (current filters/sort applied) vs 'export full table' as distinct actions. Postico's biggest missing-feature complaint is weak export — an easy surpass.

findings.title: Paste connection URL to create + copy URI (both)
findings.detail: Beekeeper parses pasted database URLs into the form; Postico has 'New Server from URL…' and a terminal URL scheme. Constantly used because credentials arrive as postgres:// strings. Beyond (qwry roadmap already has both directions): also accept psql -h ... -U ... flag strings and .env lines (DATABASE_URL=...), and offer 'Copy URI ▸ redacted / with password' from the connection menu.

findings.title: Read-only connection mode (Postico)
findings.detail: A per-connection read-only flag that blocks writes — documented, and beloved for production safety. Beyond: enforce via 'SET default_transaction_read_only = on' at connect (server-enforced, not just UI), show a persistent RO badge on tab strip + grid (cells say why they're read-only, matching qwry's ideology), and allow per-connection colors (both apps offer connection colors; prod=red is the universal idiom).

findings.title: Connection niceties: pgpass, preconnect scripts for IAM, host whitespace trimming (Postico)
findings.detail: Postico reads ~/.pgpass (2.0.5), supports pre-connect shell scripts for AWS RDS IAM / Redshift / Azure Entra token generation (2.1), and even auto-trims whitespace from pasted hostnames (2.2.3 — the definition of a small affordance). Beyond: qwry should read .pgpass and pg_service.conf, support a preconnect command whose stdout becomes the password (covers IAM + Vault), and trim/normalize every pasted field. These make it the client that 'just works' with existing Postgres tooling.

findings.title: Startup queries per connection (Postico)
findings.detail: Run SQL automatically on connect — SET ROLE, statement_timeout, search_path. Power users use it for safety defaults. Beyond: per-connection init SQL with a visible chip when active ('ROLE analyst · timeout 30s'), plus first-class fields for the common three (role, search_path, statement_timeout) so nobody has to remember syntax.

findings.title: Favorites sync via iCloud/Dropbox + nested groups + sidebar filtering (Postico)
findings.detail: Connection favorites live in a file syncable via iCloud/Drive, organized in nested groups, filterable; ⇧⌘F filters the sidebar table list. Beyond: store connections as a plain JSON file in an app-support dir (user can symlink into any sync), secrets in macOS Keychain only, groups with colors; sidebar filter with fuzzy match bound to a single keystroke when the sidebar is focused.

findings.title: Destructive-action safety: ⌘⌫ to confirm, Return disabled (Postico)
findings.detail: Delete confirmations deliberately disable Return as the confirm key and require ⌘⌫ — you cannot enter-spam your way into data loss. A signature mac-native correctness touch. Beyond: adopt ⌘⌫ in qwry's DangerModal, escalate to type-the-table-name for TRUNCATE/DROP on tables above a row-count threshold, and always show the exact SQL that will run inside the modal.

findings.title: Silent, never-interrupting updates (Postico)
findings.detail: 'Postico will never interrupt you with an update notification' — updates download in background, apply on relaunch, channel selectable. Users explicitly praise the absence of nag. Beyond: Tauri updater staged on quit, a subtle dot on the app menu when an update is waiting, changelog viewable on demand only. Anti-nag is on-brand for latency-is-the-feature.

findings.title: View columns show source-table tooltips; partitioned tables grouped (Postico 2.3.x)
findings.detail: Hovering a view's column header reveals which base table it comes from; partitions nest under their parent in the sidebar. Both are 'the app understands Postgres' moments. Beyond: qwry already resolves column origins for edit-from-SQL — expose it as header tooltips on every query result (origin table.column, type, nullability), and group partitions under parents with an aggregate row-count rollup.

findings.title: Value generators: UUIDv7 command (Postico 2.1)
findings.detail: An 'insert UUIDv7' command for cell editing — tiny, modern, users noticed. Beyond: 'Insert value ▸' in the cell editor and grid context menu: uuid v4/v7, now()/today, DEFAULT, NULL, random string — plus the same as editor snippets. Cheap density.

findings.title: Keyboard shortcut discoverability + remapping (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: A built-in shortcuts reference in Help, and every shortcut remappable via an INI config; optional vim mode with .beekeeper.vimrc support. Postico documents a full shortcut map (⌘0/⌥⌘0 toggle sidebars, ⌥⌘F filter, ⌘. cancel, ⌥⇥ literal tab in cells...). Keyboard-first is qwry ideology — discoverability is the missing half. Beyond: a ⌘/ cheat-sheet overlay filtered by focused surface, a keymap.json for remapping, and optional CodeMirror vim mode.

findings.title: Transaction awareness in the shell (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: Beekeeper detects an open transaction and reserves the connection for that tab; a manual-transaction mode gives explicit BEGIN/COMMIT control. Prevents the classic 'idle in transaction on a pooled connection' foot-gun. Beyond: a status-bar transaction chip (idle / in-tx / error-in-tx, with elapsed time) with one-click COMMIT/ROLLBACK, per-tab session pinning when BEGIN is detected, and a warning when closing a tab that holds an open transaction — never lose work includes uncommitted transactions.

findings.title: Privacy mode for screen sharing (Beekeeper 5.2)
findings.detail: One toggle blurs/hides sensitive data during demos/screenshares. Users share DB screens constantly; this got outsized praise. Beyond: global toggle that masks cell values, connection hostnames, and row counts with one shortcut; per-column 'always redact' marks persisted per table. Instant on/off, no re-query.

findings.title: Complaint census — Beekeeper: Electron sluggishness is the #1 gripe
findings.detail: GitHub #135/#752 and reviews: 1200+ tables take ~1min to load the sidebar, 7.9k rows ≈ 7s to render, window resize/scroll freezes, and users explicitly note 'Sequel Pro and TablePlus show none of this lag... Beekeeper is Electron'. 5.4 needed a '55× UI performance tune-up'. Validation for qwry: the two invariants (never slow at any scale) are precisely the wedge; keep introspection scoped (qwry's FUNCS-on-every-connect roadmap item is the same disease) and publish honest perf numbers vs Beekeeper as marketing.

findings.title: Complaint census — Beekeeper: editing requires a primary key
findings.detail: 'Beekeeper only supports editing tables with primary keys' (SQLite rowid excepted) — a recurring user complaint. Postico is also PK-dependent. Beyond: qwry can edit PK-less Postgres tables via ctid within a guarded transaction (SELECT ... WHERE ctid = ... FOR UPDATE, verify old values match before UPDATE), with a clear 'editing via physical row id — re-verify after vacuum' notice. That single capability leapfrogs every mainstream client, and read-only cells that say why (no PK, no ctid trace) already fit qwry's ideology.

findings.title: Complaint census — Postico: export/ERD/Windows gaps and the query-file regression
findings.detail: Recurring Postico complaints: weak export options (CSV-centric, no JSON/Excel from results), no table-relationship/ERD view, no multi-table compare, macOS-only, and the Postico 2 forced query-file model (#698). Users forgive all of it because the app is fast and native — proof that feel buys enormous goodwill. Beyond: qwry inherits the native-speed goodwill via Tauri; closing export (streaming multi-format) + a lightweight FK-graph peek (not a full ERD editor — just 'what references this table' in the inspector) removes the two most-cited reasons Postico users keep TablePlus around.

findings.title: Find bar in editor + ⌘F inside SQL preview popups (Postico)
findings.detail: Postico replaced its Find Panel with an inline Find Bar (2.0 RC6) and even made the SQL-preview popup ⌘F-searchable (2.0 RC1) — find works in every text surface, no exceptions. That consistency is what 'mature' means. Beyond: qwry's roadmap find-system (⌘F scoped to focused surface, identical chrome in editor/grid/inspector/JsonTree) is exactly right; extend it to DDL views, changes panel, and history panel so ⌘F literally never no-ops anywhere in the app.

findings.title: Cell-editing keyboard grammar (Postico)
findings.detail: ⇥/⇧⇥ commit-and-move right/left, ↩ commits, Esc discards, ⌥⇥ inserts a literal tab, ⌥↩ inserts a newline, ⇧⌘N new row, ⌘D duplicate row(s). The complete, documented grammar is why data entry in Postico feels like a spreadsheet. Beyond: implement the full grammar including the ⌥-escape hatches for literal tab/newline (almost no client has these), plus Enter-then-move-down as a preference, and make every one of these discoverable in the cell context menu with shortcut labels.

findings.title: Add-row appears at top despite appending (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: The '+' add-row button places the new row at the top of the viewport 'for convenience despite being appended' — a small honest-UX compromise users appreciate on big tables. Beyond: new rows pinned in a distinct 'staged inserts' section above the grid until applied, each with green tint and inline validation (NOT NULL columns without defaults highlighted before you even try to save).

findings.title: Zen mode + per-surface font zoom (Beekeeper)
findings.detail: A distraction-free full-window editor mode, and ⌘⇧./⌘⇧, font-size control; Postico has ⌘+/⌘- global. Small comfort features that show up in reviews. Beyond: ⌘+/- zoom that scales editor AND grid density coherently (row height steps: compact/normal/comfortable), persisted per user.
